config.title: Build OpenAPI documented REST service

intro.title: Build OpenAPI documented REST service
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple REST API service for managing a list of books, using Node.js and Express. You will learn how to create endpoints for adding, retrieving, and deleting books, and how to document them with OpenAPI. The core concept is using the OpenAPI specification to define your API's structure, which helps in generating clear documentation and validating requests. You'll work with JavaScript, Express for routing, and a library like Swagger UI to visualize your API documentation. By the end, you'll have a documented REST service that is easy to understand and test.
intro.usecase: OpenAPI documented REST services are foundational to modern API-driven applications like e-commerce platforms, banking systems, and SaaS products. For example, when you use a payment gateway like Stripe or a weather service API, developers rely on OpenAPI documentation to understand endpoints, request formats, and authentication. This documentation enables frontend developers to build dashboards that display transaction histories or mobile apps that fetch real-time data, while backend teams maintain clear contracts between microservices. Implementing OpenAPI ensures your API is discoverable, testable, and integrable across teams and third-party consumers.

objectives: Initialize a Node.js project with Express for REST service development
Implement route handlers for CRUD operations on a sample resource
Configure middleware to parse JSON request bodies
Integrate Swagger UI to visualize API documentation
Construct OpenAPI specification for API endpoints
Apply validation schemas to request parameters and bodies
Bind route definitions to corresponding controller functions
Render API documentation through automated OpenAPI generation

steps.title: Import Express and required modules
steps.instruction: Import Express, swagger-ui-express, and swagger-jsdoc modules at the top of your file.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. You'll need three separate imports.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express, swagger-ui-express, and swagger-jsdoc modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: Your file will have the necessary imports to build an Express server with OpenAPI documentation capabilities.
successCriteria: Express, swagger-ui-express, and swagger-jsdoc modules are imported using require()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've imported Express, swagger-ui-express, AND swagger-jsdoc modules.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're importing all three modules: Express, swagger-ui-express, and swagger-jsdoc.

steps.title: Initialize Express application
steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance by calling the Express function and assigning it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the imported Express module to create the app instance.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an Express app instance
const app = express();
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express application instance is created and ready for configuration.
successCriteria: An Express app instance is created and assigned to a constant named 'app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling the express() function and assigning the result to 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Express app instance wasn't created correctly. Review how to initialize an Express application.

steps.title: Configure middleware for JSON parsing
steps.instruction: Add the Express JSON middleware to your app using app.use() to enable parsing of JSON request bodies.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with express.json() as the middleware function.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will be able to parse JSON data from incoming HTTP requests.
successCriteria: The app.use() method is called with express.json() as the middleware.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using app.use() with express.json() as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. You need to add the JSON middleware using app.use(express.json()).

steps.title: Define OpenAPI specification options
steps.instruction: Create a constant named 'swaggerOptions' that contains an object with the swagger-jsdoc configuration. The object should have an 'apis' property set to an array containing './routes/*.js' and an 'swaggerDefinition' property with an 'info' object containing 'title', 'version', and 'description' fields.
steps.hint: Define a constant variable and assign it an object with the required properties. The 'apis' array tells swagger-jsdoc where to find your route files.
steps.expectedOutcome: A configuration object is created with the structure needed for swagger-jsdoc to generate OpenAPI documentation.
successCriteria: Constant 'swaggerOptions' is defined with an object containing 'apis' array and 'swaggerDefinition.info' object with title, version, and description.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your object has both 'apis' and 'swaggerDefinition' properties with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The configuration object isn't quite right. Make sure you're creating a constant named 'swaggerOptions' with the required properties.

steps.title: Generate OpenAPI specification
steps.instruction: Call the swaggerJsdoc function with your OpenAPI options configuration to generate the OpenAPI specification object.
steps.hint: Use the swaggerJsdoc function you imported earlier, passing your options object as an argument.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: generating a configuration object
const config = generateConfig(options);
steps.expectedOutcome: The OpenAPI specification object is created from your configuration options.
successCriteria: The swaggerJsdoc function is called with your OpenAPI options, generating the specification object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're calling swaggerJsdoc with your options object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The OpenAPI specification wasn't generated correctly. Remember to call swaggerJsdoc with your configuration options.

steps.title: Set up Swagger UI route
steps.instruction: Configure the /api-docs route to serve the Swagger UI with the generated spec using app.use()
steps.hint: Use app.use() with the route path and swaggerUi.serve, swaggerUi.setup()
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: serving static files with Express
app.use('/static', express.static('public'))
steps.expectedOutcome: The /api-docs route will serve the Swagger UI interface when the application runs
successCriteria: app.use() is called with '/api-docs' route and swaggerUi.serve/swaggerUi.setup()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using app.use() with the correct route path and both swaggerUi.serve and swaggerUi.setup() methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Swagger UI route isn't properly configured. You need to use app.use() to serve the documentation at the /api-docs endpoint.

steps.title: Create in-memory data store
steps.instruction: Initialize an array to act as an in-memory database for items, storing it in a variable named 'items'.
steps.hint: Declare a variable using 'const' and assign it an empty array [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating an in-memory data store
const users = [];
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a variable named 'items' that holds an empty array, ready to store item data.
successCriteria: Variable 'items' is declared and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared a variable named 'items' and assigned it an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Please create a variable named 'items' and set it to an empty array [].

steps.title: Implement GET /items endpoint
steps.instruction: Add a GET route at '/items' that returns all items from the data store as a JSON response.
steps.hint: Use app.get() to define the route. Inside the route handler, use res.json() to send the items array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will have a GET endpoint at '/items' that returns all stored items in JSON format.
successCriteria: A GET route is defined at '/items' that returns the items array using res.json().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using app.get() with '/items' as the route and returning the items array with res.json().
steps.feedbackWrong: The GET /items endpoint isn't implemented correctly. You need to define a route that responds to GET requests at '/items' and returns the items array as JSON.

steps.title: Implement POST /items endpoint
steps.instruction: Add a POST route at /items that accepts JSON data and adds it to the data store. The route should generate a unique ID for the new item and respond with the created item.
steps.hint: Use app.post() to handle POST requests. Access the request body via req.body. Generate an ID using the current timestamp or a simple increment. Push the new item into the items array and respond with status 201 and the created item.
steps.expectedOutcome: A POST route at /items that accepts JSON payloads, generates IDs for new items, adds them to the items array, and returns the created item with status 201.
successCriteria: POST route at /items is defined, accepts JSON data, generates unique IDs, adds items to the data store, and responds with status 201 and the created item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your POST endpoint generates an ID, adds the item to the items array, and responds with status 201.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint is missing or incomplete. Check that you're using app.post(), handling the request body, generating an ID, updating the items array, and sending the correct response.

steps.title: Add JSDoc comments to endpoints
steps.instruction: Add a JSDoc comment block above the GET /items endpoint with OpenAPI annotations to document it.
steps.hint: Use /** ... */ syntax and include @swagger or @openapi tag with endpoint details.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example JSDoc for an endpoint
/**
 * @swagger
 * /items:
 *   get:
 *     summary: Get all items
 *     responses:
 *       200:
 *         description: List of items
 */
steps.expectedOutcome: The GET /items endpoint will have a JSDoc comment with OpenAPI annotations above it.
successCriteria: A JSDoc comment block with @swagger or @openapi tag is added above the GET /items endpoint.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but make sure it's a proper JSDoc block (/** ... */) with @swagger or @openapi tag and endpoint details.
steps.feedbackWrong: The GET /items endpoint still lacks JSDoc documentation. Add a /** ... */ comment block with OpenAPI annotations above it.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Start the Express server by calling app.listen() on port 3000 and log a startup message.
steps.hint: Use app.listen(port, callback) where the callback logs a message like 'Server running on port 3000'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen on port 3000 and log a message when started.
successCriteria: app.listen() is called with port 3000 and a callback that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a callback that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server hasn't been started yet. Use app.listen() with port 3000 and a logging callback.

steps.title: Test the API and documentation
steps.instruction: Run the Express server and test the GET /items endpoint using your browser or an API client.
steps.hint: Start the server with node app.js, then open a browser to http://localhost:3000/items to see the empty items array.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server starts successfully and returns an empty array when you visit http://localhost:3000/items in your browser.
successCriteria: The server is running and the GET /items endpoint returns a JSON array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: The server may have started, but check if the endpoint returns the expected JSON array.
steps.feedbackWrong: Make sure you've added the app.listen call and started the server with node app.js.
